items.title: Payment demanded for private 'Grundstücksregister' entry
items.computation: The letter prints an explicit calendar date for payment: 01.12.2026. No period to count and no deemed-delivery rule applies since this is a private company, not an authority; the date is simply taken as written. 1 December 2026 is a Tuesday, not a weekend or public holiday in NRW, so no shift under § 193 BGB is needed.

warnings: This has the hallmarks of the well-known 'fake Grundbuch/Gewerbeauskunft' scam pattern: a private GmbH uses official-sounding branding (a shield/cross emblem, the word 'Grundstücksregister', 'Eintragung') to mimic a real land-registry (Grundbuchamt) notice and bill the owner for an entry nobody requested.

The letter itself admits this is only an 'Angebot' (offer) and that 'ein Vertrag kommt erst durch die Zahlung zustande' (a contract only comes into being once you pay) and that the entry 'steht in keinem Zusammenhang mit dem amtlichen Grundbuch' (has nothing to do with the official land register) — so there is currently no payment obligation at all, and paying would create one where none existed before.

Genuine entries in the German Grundbuch are made only by the competent Amtsgericht (land registry court) and are never invoiced by a private company in this manner; recommend not paying and, if in doubt, contacting the local Grundbuchamt directly using independently verified contact details.
No legal-remedy instructions (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung) are given, consistent with this being a private commercial offer rather than an official administrative decision.
